whatsHappening.background: Venezuela is facing a long-running humanitarian crisis rooted in economic collapse, inflation, weakened public services, political repression, and mass migration. Since 2014, families have struggled to afford food, medicine, health care, education, and safe water. In 2026, UNICEF says 7.9 million people inside Venezuela, including 3.9 million children, need humanitarian assistance.

parties.name: UN Agencies
parties.description: UNICEF, UNHCR, WFP, and partners support children, migrants, and vulnerable families.

timeline.description: Economic collapse accelerates and humanitarian needs begin growing.
Millions leave Venezuela in one of the world’s largest displacement crises.
Needs remain high as inflation, weak services, and funding gaps continue.

civilianImpact.experiences: Children and families face malnutrition, preventable disease, unsafe water, violence, exploitation, and interrupted education. Migration has separated many families, while shortages of doctors, teachers, medicine, and basic services make daily life harder for people who remain inside the country.

image.alt: Children receiving food support in Venezuela

howToHelp.summary: Donations help keep food, health care, water, education, and protection services running for vulnerable families. Because Venezuela remains underfunded, steady support matters.
